title: Interoperability surface and observability hooks for terraform primitives
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a proposed interoperability surface (variables and outputs) for Terraform primitives that back private deployments (VPC + IAM + cluster primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS). It also defines lightweight observability hooks, compatibility/versioning patterns, and a practical upgrade/canary playbook.

Scope:
- VPC/network primitives and their outputs for routing/peering and logging buckets.
- IAM primitives for service roles, cross-account trust, service account annotation plumbing for Kubernetes.
- Cluster primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS: bootstrap outputs (kubeconfig, OIDC provider, nodepool identities).
- Upgrade and compatibility steps for module consumers and infra teams.
- Observability / telemetry tags and outputs to make runtime debugging and rollout validation easier.

Design principles (short):
- Minimal, explicit contract: expose only stable primitives that are necessary for downstream modules.
- Provider-agnostic naming where possible (eg. cluster_endpoint, cluster_oidc_url) so consumer code can be shared.
- Backwards-compatible extension: add new outputs/variables, never remove or rename without a migration path.
- Single source of truth for semantic version: primitive_module_version (string) injected into resources as tags/labels.
- Observability-first: include lightweight hooks so rollout/upgrade CI/CD can assert signals quickly.

Primitive interface proposals (examples):
1) network/vpc primitive (module input/output sketch)
  inputs (important, minimal):
    - name_prefix: string (required)
    - environment: string (required, e.g., staging/prod)
    - cidr_blocks: list(string) or object with zones -> cidr mapping
    - enable_flow_logs: bool (default true)
    - flow_logs_bucket: optional string (if omitted module creates bucket and returns name)
    - tags: map(string) (merged with base tags)
    - primitive_module_version: string (used by module to tag resources)
  outputs (stable):
    - vpc_id: string
    - private_subnet_ids: list(string) (ordered by availability zone)
    - public_subnet_ids: list(string)
    - route_table_ids: list(string)
    - nat_gateway_ids: list(string) or empty list if none
    - flow_logs_bucket_name: string
    - network_resource_tags: map(string) (canonical set used by module)
    - primitive_module_version: string (output the module version)

2) iam primitive
  inputs:
    - name_prefix
    - service_account_mappings: optional list(object) (k8s namespace/name -> iam role mapping)
    - extra_policies: list(string) (policy ARNs or JSON blobs)
  outputs:
    - iam_role_arns: map(string) keyed by logical role name
    - iam_policies: map(string) JSON strings for inline policies when needed
    - iam_oidc_provider_arn: string (if created)

3) cluster primitive (provider-agnostic outputs)
  inputs:
    - cluster_name
    - control_plane_config (map)
    - kubelet_sa_mappings (to attach IAM roles/serviceAccounts)
    - network_inputs: accepts vpc module outputs (see above)
    - primitive_module_version
  outputs:
    - cluster_name: string
    - cluster_endpoint: string
    - cluster_ca_certificate: string (base64)
    - kubeconfig_path_hint: string (local path that bootstrap scripts write for local CI)
    - provider_oidc_url: string (for EKS/OIDC or GKE Workload Identity)
    - cluster_nodepool_labels: map(string) (first-class labels suggested by module)
    - cluster_resource_tags: map(string)
    - primitive_module_version: string

Observability hooks and lightweight telemetry (why):
- Rollouts fail fast if we can assert infra-level signals: subnets created, flow logs enabled, OIDC present, roles assumeable.
- Hooks should be cheap and not require customers to adopt a specific monitoring stack.

Proposed observable outputs and tags (convention):
- Tags applied to every named resource: {"redwood:component": "primitive-name", "redwood:environment": "${var.environment}", "redwood:primitive_version": "${var.primitive_module_version}", "redwood:owner": "${var.owner || \"unknown\"}"} (owner optional)
- Module outputs that feed CI/CD validation: vpc_id, flow_logs_bucket_name, iam_role_arns, provider_oidc_url, cluster_endpoint. These are emitted as stdout in the plan/apply CI step for machine parsing.
- An optional prometheus-friendly metric emitter (pushgateway step in CI) that posts: primitive_deploy_duration_seconds, primitive_apply_errors_total, primitive_validation_failures_total. The module should surface times in outputs when invoked by CI wrapper (eg. last_apply_duration_seconds).
- Upload of a small JSON manifest to central storage for each apply (can be disabled): {module, version, outputs_summary, timestamp} so rollout can audit what changed without parsing terraform state directly.

Compatibility & versioning pattern:
- Every primitive module must export primitive_module_version output and accept primitive_module_version input.
- Semantic versioning for module interface only (semver-like but treat additions as minor/patch allowed):
  - patch: internal implementation changes, state-compatible.
  - minor: additive outputs/optional variables, should not break consumers.
  - major: breaking change to variable/output names or semantics; requires explicit migration runbook and migration tool if state changes are needed.
- A compatibility-check job (CI) that:
  - runs terraform init/plan in a read-only workspace against a saved state snapshot,
  - runs a lightweight tf-diff parser to ensure no output renames or type changes,
  - fails if a delta includes removal or type-change of outputs that consumers depend on.

Upgrade / Canary playbook (practical steps):
1) Developer/owner increments module version and opens PR with change notes + impact matrix.
2) CI compatibility job runs automatically and posts results to PR (link to JIRA ticket if failing).
3) If minor/patch: create a canary workspace in staging: apply module with same inputs but module source pointed to PR branch.
   - Verify smoke signals: can we assume the iam roles? are subnets reachable? flow logs enabled? run the validation tests below.
4) Canary validation tests (automated):
   - TF smoke: plan/apply/plan idempotency check
   - IAM assume test: service in that account should be able to assume role and list expected resources
   - Network test: launch tiny echo pod (k8s) and curl metadata endpoints across AZs, confirm SNAT from NAT gateways where expected
   - Telemetry test: check the manifest uploaded and metrics emitted to pushgateway (if enabled)
   - Cluster bootstrap test: kubeconfig works, deploy minimal chart that uses SA->IAM bindings and assert token behavior
5) Canary duration: 24–72 hours depending on blast radius. During that time run synthetic traffic if the primitive touches runtime infra.
6) If all green, promote module: update module registry tag and roll to broader non-prod workspaces.
7) For major changes: produce a migration plan: state transforms (using terraform state mv + scripted transforms), shadow resource creation, dual-write period, and a final cutover with state reconciliation.

Rollback & recovery patterns:
- Always take tfstate backup snapshots before apply (CI must fail if backup cannot be uploaded).
- For destructive plans: require manual approval in CI and an explicit backout PR that reverts to previous module tag.
- If apply partially fails and leaves resources in an inconsistent state: run targeted apply with the previous module tag and minimal inputs to reconcile state; use state import for resources created outside TF.
- If new module version requires resource replacement: prefer a pattern that creates new resources alongside old and shifts traffic using DNS/route tables, then tear down old after validation.

Testing matrix & harness suggestions:
- Local developer mode: thin wrapper that runs terraform validate, fmt, and a tainted example apply in the dockerized sandbox.
- CI gating tests:
  - unit: terraform validate + custom linters (variable naming, output docs present)
  - integration: plan against recorded minimal state (mocked cloud)
  - canary: apply to staging project with deterministic inputs
  - e2e: for cluster primitives, run conformance/cilium or networking smoke tests
- Test data: provide a set of canonical tfvars for small/medium/large footprints. Use these in CI matrix to catch scale/behavior differences.

Migration helpers & scripts (implementation notes):
- migration/transform.sh: wrapper to run terraform state mv commands annotated with JIRA ticket and dry-run flag.
- output-compat-checker: Node/Python script that loads two output JSONs (old vs new) and emits a compatibility score and highlights breaking changes.
- state-snapshot-uploader: small utility that zips tfstate and uploads to internal artifact storage for audit.

Example consumer-safe naming conventions to document in README (so downstream teams can rely on stable keys):
- network.vpc_id -> module.network.vpc_id (string)
- network.private_subnet_ids -> module.network.private_subnet_ids[*] (list)
- iam.iam_role_arns.webhook -> module.iam.iam_role_arns["webhook"]
- cluster.cluster_endpoint -> module.cluster.cluster_endpoint
- cluster.provider_oidc_url -> module.cluster.provider_oidc_url

Open questions / TODOs (callouts for reviewers):
- Do we want modules to emit a lightweight manifest JSON to a central S3/GCS bucket by default or opt-in? (privacy / compliance tradeoff)
- How do we standardize the prometheus metric names / push endpoint across CI systems? propose a small RFC.
- Owner field: should module require owner input or optional and filled by CI? (helps for tagging and paging)
- Cross-account patterns: define a canonical pattern for external-id usage in cross-account IAM role creation to avoid ambiguous trust boundaries.
- GKE/AKS differences: some outputs (workload identity artifacts) are provider-specific; propose provider neutral outputs plus provider_extra map for provider-only bits.

Appendix: quick checklist for module authors (to be copied into module README):
- [ ] Export primitive_module_version and accept it as a variable.
- [ ] Document every output with type and stability note.
- [ ] Add default tags and allow tag merging.
- [ ] Add acceptance test tfvars (small footprint) and wire into CI.
- [ ] Ensure plan compatibility job runs and fails fast if outputs change semantically.
- [ ] Add a migration example for any major change (state mv examples).

TL;DR:
Keep the surface small and stable, tag everything with primitive_version, make outputs parseable by CI, provide a canary workspace and simple validation harness that tests assume/authorize/networking/manifest signals, and require an explicit migration plan for anything that renames or changes output types.

Notes-to-self: put a lightweight template for the manifest upload (json schema), and a starter compatibility-checker README in tools/compatibility-checker. Link the PR once created.

-- end of draft --
